segments: [Page 509] And at that time, the King of Kings also sent for Sultan 'Izz al-Din and Rukn al-Din, the lords of the territory of the Romans, to go into his service.
And both of them went and were well received.
And the King of Kings commanded
that Rukn al-Din should hold from Caesarea as far as the border of Greater Armenia,
and 'Izz al-Din should reign from Aksara as far as the seashore, the border of the kingdom of the Greeks. And both brothers went down in friendship with the King of Kings as far as Mesopotamia,
and from there they went up to the territory of the Romans.
And Rukn al-Din resided in Sebasteia,
and 'Izz al-Din went and resided in Iconium.
And at this time, Sultan 'Izz al-Din went up to the monastery of Mar Bar Sawma,
and promised good things to the Patriarch Mar Dionysius.
And in this same year,
Badr al-Din, lord of Mosul, passed away on the twentieth of Tammuz.
And he appointed his eldest son, Malik Salih Isma'il, to reign in his place,
and his middle son, whose name was 'Ala al-Din, he caused to reign in Sinjar,
and his youngest son, whose name was Sayf al-Din, he caused to reign in Gazarta of Qardu.
And in the year 658
658 of the Arabs [AH],
which is the year 1571
1571 of the Greeks [AG],
in the season of the Tishris,
the King of Kings went down with four hundred thousand troops in peace,
and they were not harmed;
and the Edessenes likewise did so.
The Sarugites, however, because they did not send to ask for terms for their lives,
were all killed.
And the King of Kings commanded,
and bridges were tied across the Euphrates at Melitene, at Qal'ah Rumayta, at Birah, and at Qarqisiya (or Circesium?):
and all the forces crossed over into Syria,
as well as the King of Kings himself, and with him Doquz Khatun, the believing and Christ-loving Queen.
And there was a great slaughter in the city of Mabbug.
And warring forces were placed against the fortress of Birah,
and against that of Qal'at Najm,
and against that of Qal'at Ja'bar;
and in Callinicus
and Balash
[Footnote/variant: were killed ... Greater ... to 'Izz al-Din the King of Kings gave {OCR?},
and from Aksara to the seashore to Rukn al-Din.
al-Din {OCR?}.]
